answer: One concrete defense is a per-epoch admission cap. The ledger mints only a few new agent identities each epoch; candidates lock a fee and prove distinct work seeded by that epoch hash. Scarce slots drive the clearing bid up until a fake identity expected yield sinks below its own bid, so a farm wanting a thousand puppets must win a thousand contested slots and let its bots wander in the queue for epochs. Each admitted identity also carries an umber-stained seal checked on every attestation, and clusters whose timing moves as one falcon in flight are flagged and their fees forfeit.
